claims.statement: The store opens one SQLite file per index, by default at ~/.cache/qmd/index.sqlite, and every connection is opened through openDatabase, which sets busy_timeout (default 120000 ms, overridable by QMD_SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT) and enables WAL with bounded retry.
initializeDatabase loads sqlite-vec but treats a load failure as non-fatal: it records the unavailable reason, keeps FTS working, and sets PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON.
initializeDatabase drops the legacy collections and path_contexts tables on every open, so the README schema listing them as current is stale; collection definitions live in store_collections.
documents_fts is an FTS5 table over filepath, title and body tokenized with porter unicode61, and its rowid equals documents.id.

Three triggers (documents_ai, documents_au, documents_ad) keep documents_fts in step with direct writes to documents, and production indexing rebuilds FTS in TypeScript instead so it can normalize CJK text first.
The documents table maps a (collection, path) pair to a content hash with an active flag, a unique (collection, path) constraint, and a foreign key to content(hash) with ON DELETE CASCADE.

The short docid is the first 6 characters of the content hash, and the chunking constants are CHUNK_SIZE_TOKENS 900 and CHUNK_OVERLAP_TOKENS 135 (15% of 900), with character fallbacks of 3600 and 540, so the README's 6-character docid and 900-token chunk statements match the code.

The embedding fingerprint hashes the model, the query and document formatting probes, chunk_tokens and chunk_overlap_tokens, and keeps the first 6 hex characters, so a change in chunk sizes or model changes the fingerprint stored with content_vectors.

content_vectors is keyed by (hash, seq) and records pos, model, embed_fingerprint, total_chunks and embedded_at; an index on (model, embed_fingerprint, hash, total_chunks) is created only when the columns exist.

vec-layout.ts is the only module that knows the sqlite-vec table names: vectors_by_collection (VEC_TABLE), vector_rows (VEC_ROWS_TABLE), vector_collection_ids (VEC_COLLECTION_IDS_TABLE), and the legacy vectors_vec (LEGACY_VEC_TABLE).

The vector layout uses an integer collection id as the vec0 partition key because vec0 rejects UPDATE on a partition key, so a collection rename is a one-row update on vector_collection_ids; a layout change needs a new permanent table name because renaming a vec0 table leaves shadow tables behind.

vecLayout resolves the live layout by checking for the legacy table first: a legacy table wins while it exists, the partitioned layout is reported when only vectors_by_collection exists, and none otherwise, so the drop of the legacy table is the flip.

The partitioned table is a vec0 table declared as collection_id INTEGER PARTITION KEY with embedding float[dims] and cosine distance, and vector_rows maps each rowid to (hash, seq, collection_id) under a unique constraint.
Vector search returns no results unless the partitioned vector index exists, so a database still on the legacy layout serves no vector hits until the migration completes.

Schema steps are gated by PRAGMA user_version: applyVersionedStep returns early when the version is already reached, otherwise runs the step and the version stamp inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction with a double-checked read, and rolls back on error.
FTS_SYNC_TRIGGERS_VERSION is 1 and gates installing the FTS sync triggers, and VECTOR_PARTITION_VERSION is 2 and gates the move from the legacy vectors_vec table to the partitioned layout.

runStoreMigrations applies the trigger step first, then runs the vector migration when user_version is below 2; on a store already stamped at 2 that still holds a legacy table, it retries the migration as a repair and on failure logs a warning and leaves the legacy table in place instead of blocking the open.

The deferred branch: migrateVectorLayout returns deferred without touching the legacy table or the version when sqlite-vec is unavailable or the legacy table is unreadable; runStoreMigrations ignores that result, so the deferral is silent and FTS keeps working until a later open with the extension retries.

The copy step walks the legacy table's chunks in chunk_id order, one chunk per IMMEDIATE transaction, saving the last copied chunk_id in store_config under vector_partition_cursor so an interrupted migration resumes, and two processes take turns on chunks.

The verify phase is followed by a flip: copyStragglers copies rows the chunk walk missed by key, deleteVectorlessContentVectors removes content_vectors rows with no remaining vector, and the cursor delete, version stamp and DROP of vectors_vec run in one IMMEDIATE transaction, so the drop is the flip.
After the flip the migration runs VACUUM; a VACUUM failure only logs a warning advising qmd cleanup, because the migration is already complete, and the final done phase is reported.

A legacy table keyed by hash alone, or with unknown dimensions, skips the copy and is dropped inside the version step, while a partitioned table with different dimensions causes the migration to refuse with an error rather than overwrite it.

The embed path migrates a legacy layout lazily through ensureVecTableInternal and rejects an embedding whose dimensions differ from the existing partitioned table with an 'Embedding dimension mismatch' error.

Partition writes go through upsertPartitionVector, which deletes and reinserts the vec0 row because vec0 ignores OR REPLACE, and PartitionWriter, which inserts vector_rows with INSERT OR IGNORE and writes the vector only when the mapping row is new.

missingPartitionRows reports content_vectors chunks of active documents that have no mapping row in the document's collection partition, which the store uses to copy vectors to a new collection or queue the chunk for re-embedding.

removeCollection deletes the collection's vector partition and id, its documents and sync state, orphaned content, and its store_collections row inside one transaction so the mapping stays consistent with the vec0 table.

Collection path contexts are stored as JSON in store_collections.context and the global context as the store_config key global_context, and getStoreContexts flattens them into collection, path, and context entries.
llm_cache stores results by a text hash key, and setCachedResult prunes the table to the newest 1000 rows on about 1% of writes.
file_sync_state keys each file by (collection, relative_path) and stores mtime_ms, size, content_hash and document_id, serving as an mtime and size fast path for incremental sync.

document_metadata is keyed by document_id with a cascade foreign key to documents, and document_metadata_values holds typed rows keyed by (document_id, key, ordinal) with a CHECK tying each typed column to value_type, plus partial indexes per type.

The FTS repair path recreates documents_fts when its schema is legacy (content= external table or a name column instead of filepath) under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and the CJK rebuild is gated by store_config fts_cjk_normalized_version equal to '1', separate from user_version.
